- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 15–25% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp spike in true outcome, model often overshoots in the following 3–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 20–40% of the spike’s magnitude.  
- Model consistently underestimates long-term (15+ day) trends; for 30-day forecasts, add 1.5–2x the average recent 7-day volatility to the mean.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply a “reversion bias” correction: subtract 10–20% from forecast if sentiment flips from + to - or vice versa.  
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; for 30-day forecasts, smooth sentiment impact by averaging last 3 sentiment values before applying correction.
